claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - Alex, who's 8 years old and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old and lives with you.

Now I need to ask about your residency:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand a bit more about your responsibility for Alex:

**Are you the one who provides for Alex's day-to-day needs such as food, clothes, and general care?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. I look after Alex and provide for all their day-to-day needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure actually - Alex's other parent lives with us too, so I don't know if they might already be claiming it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. It's important to clarify this because only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child.

**Could you check with Alex's other parent whether they are currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** If they are, you wouldn't be able to claim it as well (though you could agree to switch who claims it if you both prefer that). If they're not claiming it, then you may be eligible to make a claim.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I can check with them and get back to you. But assuming they're not claiming it, would I be eligible then?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, let me assess your situation assuming Alex's other parent is not currently claiming Child Benefit.

Let me review the key factors:
- You have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old (under 16)
- You live in the UK
- Alex lives with you
- You are responsible for Alex and provide for their day-to-day needs (food, clothes, and general care)

However, before I can give you a final determination, I need to ask one more important question:

**Do you have the right to reside in the UK? For example, are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled status, pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or another immigration status that gives you the right to reside here?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! Based on the information you've provided, **you would be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**, assuming that Alex's other parent is not currently claiming it.

Here's why you're eligible:

✓ **Alex is 8 years old** - under the age limit of 16 (or 20 if in approved education)
✓ **You live in the UK** and are a UK citizen - meeting residency requirements  
✓ **Alex lives with you** - satisfying the responsibility test
✓ **You provide for Alex's day-to-day needs** - further confirming you're responsible for Alex

**Important reminder:** Only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child. So please do check with Alex's other parent to confirm they're not already claiming it. If they are claiming it and you'd prefer to claim instead, you would need to agree between yourselves who should claim, and the person currently claiming would need to stop their claim before you could make a new one.

If no one is currently claiming, you can go ahead and apply for Child Benefit for Alex!
